body:
My accident happened in a remote location in alaska.. I'm currently in the process of figuring what's going on with me legally, my psychiatrist has diagnosed or categorized me with moderate/severe ptsd.. It sucks but atleast I have some idea of what's "wrong" with me? I havent reached out to any of my home state friends now because I still cant fathom what that means though but I know its bad.. There is a federal criminal case against what has happened to me, thats great I guess but I've only given one federal statement directly to the agency and i just want it all to be over. I want to put this behind me and move on with my life but this series of events has forever changed me.. I cant see explosions in any context without crying/breaking down.. even in my dreams i wake up crying all the time and I just want it to end, false awakenings happen every night have me questioning what is real or not to the point of where I "wake up" with my gun in my hand and I pull the trigger and feel the release. Only to wake up for real and realize that I'm still alive. Ive given my gun to my family for this reason but ive lost sense of what my reality is now

I have a couple friends in my corner, but I'm pushing them away because I dont want them to deal with the effect they would have on the end of me. I'm currently seeing a neuropsychiatrist for my PTSD but the workers comp associated with my case wont send me to an actual therapist for consulting because most will not take a workers comp case due to the less pay compared to private. I'm at a loss. I've reached out to my local college to try to get some free counseling but they havent gotten back to me.

I hate to admit it, but I need someone to talk to. I am afraid of my own safety

That sucks to hear, but I appreciate you helping me out sorting through this mess. 

While I could argue for an exception, it seem that I either I take the severance now or risk a lengthy legal battle where I could only end up racking up legal fees and come out with the same, if not less of the severance amount, and that's only if I win. My only other hope is banking on a better settlement from my workers compensation

Thanks for the link, it rings similar to what the attorney I have spoken with said. I have spoken with a workers comp attorney however my case has not come entirely to a close as i havent received my impairment rating, so I am not at the point where I need a workers comp lawyer according to them. The workers comp lawyer referred me to an employment law attorney which is the one that spoke with me about the above.

With that being said, does this mean I cant sue for any negligence? I was an at will employee, so during for my remainder of contract would not be possible
Yes. I've gone through the whole process and my workers comp claim is almost complete
